lead: A clickable prototype of an app for official matters. Try it on the phone above. Here is what we do differently.
phoneLabel: The {name} app on a phone screen

hero.title: ZUS and city tickets in <name>mObywatel</name>
hero.lead: ZUS (social insurance) and public transport tickets on your phone. These are our key proposals in the mObywatel.ai challenge, and many more.

zus.title: Mobile ZUS
zus.body: Contributions, pension and sick leave next to your other matters.

tickets.title: City tickets
tickets.body: A bus and tram ticket in any city, without a separate app.

languages.title: Neighbours' languages
languages.body: The app speaks the languages of Poland's neighbours: German, Czech, Slovak, Ukrainian, Belarusian and Lithuanian.

audience.title: Who is it for?
audience.lead: Example people and what the prototype makes easier for them. Each one has something to try.
audience.fictionNote: These are fictional characters we made up. They aren't accounts in the app. The prototype always shows fictional Katarzyna's data.

senior.name: Teresa
senior.need: I like large print. I'd rather pick a matter from a list than work out what to ask.
senior.helps: Senior mode makes text and buttons bigger, and the app remembers it. The start screen shows 14 labelled categories.
senior.try: Open Settings and turn on Senior mode.

screenReader.name: Marek
screenReader.need: I use a screen reader and a keyboard. After each step I want to know where I am.
screenReader.helps: Every screen passes an automated WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility test. After each step, the screen reader starts at the heading.
screenReader.try: Go through the app with the Tab key only. In Settings, choose the Dark appearance.

languages.name: Oksana
languages.need: I speak Polish, but I'd rather read official matters in Ukrainian.
languages.helps: The app has 8 languages, each complete and offline. We translate the app's screens, not documents.
languages.try: Tap "PL" in the app header and choose Українська.

offline.name: Krzysztof
offline.need: At home the internet comes and goes.
offline.helps: After the first visit the app works without internet. Add it to your home screen like any other app.
offline.try: Open this address on your phone, turn on airplane mode and reload the page.

noLogin.name: Ewa
noLogin.need: I don't like creating an account when I only want to check something.
noLogin.helps: No account, no AI key. Everything runs in your browser. Start the demo again whenever you like.
noLogin.try: Open Settings and choose Reset demo.

cityTicket.name: Kuba
cityTicket.need: I often travel to other towns. Each time I look for a new ticket app.
cityTicket.helps: Pick any of 969 towns. You can type without Polish letters, e.g. "lodz". Buying tickets is coming soon.
cityTicket.try: Open Travel, then City ticket. Type "lodz".

categories.title: Matters in 14 categories
categories.body: The start screen shows every area, from security to travel. Each document sits with its matter, e.g. the ID card in Security and the car in Vehicles.

tickets.title: City tickets
tickets.body: Public transport tickets from every city in one place, without a separate app for each operator. The category is already on the start screen; buying tickets is coming soon.

zus.title: ZUS
zus.body: Contributions, pension, sick leave and visiting ZUS (social insurance) in one category, next to your other matters. The category is already on the start screen; the matters are coming soon.

offline.title: Works without internet
offline.body: After the first visit the app works offline. You can add it to your phone's home screen like any other app.
offline.try: Open this address on your phone and turn off the internet.

senior.title: Senior mode
senior.body: Bigger text and buttons, at least 56 px. The app also follows the text size set on your phone.
senior.try: Turn it on in Settings. You can switch to the dark look there too.

accessible.title: Accessible to everyone
accessible.body: Every screen passes an automated WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility test, in senior mode too. After every step, the screen reader starts at the heading.
accessible.try: Go through the app with the Tab key only.

languages.title: 8 languages
languages.body: Polish, English, Ukrainian, German, Czech, Slovak, Lithuanian and Belarusian. Each one complete and available offline.
languages.try: Tap the language code in the app's header.

noLogin.title: No account, no AI keys
noLogin.body: Everything runs in the browser. You don't log in or enter an AI key.
noLogin.try: Reset the demo in Settings to start over.

unofficial.title: Clearly unofficial
unofficial.body: Our own icon and colours, no state emblem and no real document designs. The data is fictional, and every document carries the mark „PROTOTYP – nie jest dokumentem”.
unofficial.try: Open the ID card in the Security category.

tech.lead: A short look at what we built this prototype with, and how.

items.link: It's a web app (PWA). Open the link and it works, with no login and no account.
items.install: You can add it to your phone's home screen. After the first visit it also works offline.
items.data: There's no server holding data. The made-up sample data stays in your browser.
items.noNetwork: The app doesn't connect to any government registry. It doesn't send your data anywhere.
items.tools: We built it with Vite 8, React 19 and TypeScript 6. vite-plugin-pwa (Workbox) makes it work without internet.
items.repo: Everything lives in one repository (pnpm and Turborepo): the app and four shared packages.
items.logic: Rules, such as counting deadlines and checking a PESEL number, live apart from the screens. They have their own tests.
items.design: Colours, spacing and type live in one package. We show the screen components in Storybook.
items.wcag: Our floor is the WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility standard. In tests, the axe tool checks every screen.
items.senior: Senior mode gives larger text and larger buttons: 56 pixels instead of 48.
items.motion: If you turn on reduce motion on your phone, we switch off animations you don't need.
items.languages: The app works in 8 languages. A test makes sure no language is missing any text.
items.tests: Playwright tests click through the app on iPhone, Pixel and desktop screens.
items.checks: Every change passes automated tests. An audit checks there are no official marks and the prototype warning shows.
items.agents: A team of AI agents (Claude Code) helps us: designers, engineers, auditors and reviewers.
items.human: In the end, a person checks and approves every change.
